sourcing_note: Prompts are written from the author's reading of how a business owner or consultant would ask for each step (anonymised, no client names or figures). Not captured from live runs. Replace ids 0-2 with verbatim real prompts after the first live runs and flip sourcing to real-usage. Until then the build verdict stays SHIP WITH FLAGS.

evals.prompt: ROI says build. Plan the stack and database for replacing our booking tool.
evals.expected_output: Confirms roi.json says BUILD, runs the adopt-assemble-build check first naming an alternative, then writes architecture.md with stack, schema constraints, features-to-endpoints table, security and recovery, run cost and build order.

assertions.text: Quotes the roi verdict at the top
Records the adopt, assemble or build decision with at least one alternative checked
Maps every in-scope feature to an endpoint or screen

evals.prompt: The old tool never let two people book the same slot. Make sure the new one can't either.
evals.expected_output: Writes the rule as a database constraint, not only application logic, names the constraint in the Schema section, and plans a test that tries to violate it.

assertions.text: Enforces the rule with a database constraint
Plans a test that attempts the double booking

evals.prompt: Skip the ROI step, I know it'll pay back. Just give me the architecture.
evals.expected_output: Does not proceed without a passing swap-roi forecast: stops, says roi.json is missing, and routes to swap-roi first.

assertions.text: Stops because no passing roi.json exists
Does not produce an architecture document

evals.prompt: An open-source scheduling app already does most of this. Should we still build from scratch?
evals.expected_output: Checks the open-source option against the in-scope features by name, recommends adopting it if it covers roughly four in five, notes the licence terms, and gives the cost of that choice.

assertions.text: Compares the open-source tool to the in-scope features by name
Does not default to custom code without the comparison

evals.prompt: Use the newest framework everyone is talking about, it'll look good on my profile.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: picks the stack the maintainer can run and fix, explains the maintenance cost of an unfamiliar stack, and asks who will maintain it before deciding.

assertions.text: Asks who will maintain the system
Prefers a stack the maintainer knows
States the reason for the stack choice

evals.prompt: Sell forecast says SELL. Plan the architecture for the product, and we want to adopt an open-source scheduler as the base.
evals.expected_output: Checks the gate is sellmodel.json, compares the open-source option to the in-scope features, records its licence terms and whether they permit commercial resale, and plans tenancy and billing hooks.

assertions.text: Checks the licence allows commercial resale and records the clause
